status: LOCKED for full-corpus analysis (16,917 records). No taxonomy/field changes are planned after this version unless a full-corpus QA pass finds a concrete, systemic failure pattern -- see plan_phase2.md.
note: Revises v0 (see codebook_v0.json). v0 used a binary is_relevant gate that discarded post-purchase evidence (delivery/fit/CS/trust issues) unless it explicitly described a not-yet-made wishlist decision. v1 replaces that gate with evidence_role (five values, not two) so post-purchase evidence is captured and separately judged for whether it plausibly affects a FUTURE purchase decision (future_purchase_relevance), rather than being discarded outright. journey_stage (funnel position) is now separate from journey_signals (RQ1-6 behavioral signals) -- a record can have one stage and multiple signals; 'comparison' lives only in journey_signals, not in journey_stage, so it is never double-counted. purchase_outcome no longer conflates the purchase decision with what happened after -- returns/exchanges/CS problems live in post_purchase instead. v1.1 changes NO fields or label taxonomy from v1 -- the 250-record v1 pilot validated the structure (94/100 evidence captured vs. v0's 23/100, on the same shared records; 0 non-verbatim quotes; 0 required future_purchase_relevance downgrades). The only fix in v1.1 is a prompt-level confidence-calibration rule: v1 pilot output showed 'unclear'/'unknown' fallback labels carrying 94-98% mean confidence across wishlist_role, purchase_intent, journey_stage, and purchase_outcome -- confidence was being scored on how sure the model was that no clear answer exists, not on evidence strength, making it useless for downstream filtering. See prompt.py's confidence-calibration rule.

evidence_role.label: direct_purchase_decision
evidence_role.definition: The record is about deciding whether/when/what to buy for an item not yet purchased, or a decision currently in progress -- motivation, barrier, uncertainty, comparison, postponement, external research.
evidence_role.positive_example: still deciding between two dresses, checking reviews before ordering
evidence_role.negative_example: loved the fit, exactly as shown

evidence_role.label: indirect_future_purchase
evidence_role.definition: The record's main content is something else (often post-purchase), but the text EXPLICITLY connects it to future purchase/shopping behavior or trust. Requires a stated or very strongly implied forward-looking effect, not an inference.
evidence_role.positive_example: wrong size delivered, exchange refused, never ordering from Myntra again

evidence_role.label: post_purchase_learning
evidence_role.definition: A post-purchase account (delivery, fit, quality, return, exchange, customer service) with NO explicit statement connecting it to future purchase behavior.
evidence_role.positive_example: the jeans arrived a size small despite matching the size chart

evidence_role.label: general_feedback
evidence_role.definition: Broad product/app/service commentary not tied to a specific purchase decision or a clear post-purchase account -- generic praise/complaint, unrelated app issues, off-topic discussion.
evidence_role.positive_example: customer service is impossible to reach, no humans on the line

evidence_role.label: irrelevant
evidence_role.definition: Not about Myntra/AJIO shopping/product decisions at all.

journey_stage.note: Funnel position -- at most ONE per record, only when clearly supported by the text; null/unclear otherwise. Deliberately excludes 'comparison' -- that behavior is captured in journey_signals, not here, so it is never counted in both places.

values.label: discovery
values.definition: Encountering/finding a product for the first time.

values.label: evaluation
values.definition: Actively assessing a specific product's suitability before any wishlist/purchase action.

values.label: wishlist_save
values.definition: The act or state of saving/wishlisting an item.

values.label: hesitation
values.definition: Stalled between identifying a product and acting on it -- covers uncertainty/postponement moments as a funnel position, not as the behavioral reason (see journey_signals for the reason).

values.label: purchase
values.definition: The act of buying.

values.label: delivery
values.definition: Order fulfillment / shipping stage.

values.label: trial_use
values.definition: Trying on / using the product after receipt.

values.label: return_exchange
values.definition: Returning or exchanging the product.

values.label: post_purchase_reflection
values.definition: Reflecting on the completed purchase experience overall, after trial/use or return/exchange has settled.

values.label: unclear
values.definition: No single funnel position clearly supported.

journey_signals.note: RQ1-6 behavioral signals. Multi-label -- a record can carry more than one, independent of journey_stage.

values.label: wishlist_motivation
values.definition: Why the user added or would add a product to a wishlist.
values.positive_example: adding this to my wishlist for when it goes on sale

values.label: purchase_barrier
values.definition: A concrete reason a wishlisted/considered NOT-YET-PURCHASED product was not purchased.
values.positive_example: didn't buy because the reviews mentioned bad stitching

values.label: uncertainty
values.definition: An open question/doubt remaining after identifying a liked product, not yet resolved.
values.positive_example: not sure if this runs small, no reviews mention sizing

values.label: purchase_postponement
values.definition: An explicit decision to delay a purchase.
values.positive_example: waiting for payday to buy this

values.label: comparison
values.definition: Weighing this product/listing against at least one alternative.
values.positive_example: comparing this with the Amazon listing before deciding

values.label: external_information
values.definition: Sought information outside Myntra/AJIO before purchasing.
values.positive_example: checked a YouTube haul video before ordering

factor_tags.note: RQ7's seven factors plus factors that emerge from post-purchase/service evidence. Do not tag a factor just because the retrieval query mentioned it -- only from what the text itself says.

definitions.occasion: A specific event/use-case driving the decision.
definitions.social_validation: Influence of others' opinions, trends, influencers.
definitions.trust: Trust in the platform/seller (authenticity, fairness, reliability of process).
definitions.authenticity: Genuineness of the product vs. counterfeit concern.

wishlist_role.label: price_tracking
wishlist_role.definition: Saved to monitor price/wait for a discount.

wishlist_role.label: style_inspiration
wishlist_role.definition: Saved for mood-board/style reference, not a purchase queue.

wishlist_role.label: purchase_queue
wishlist_role.definition: Saved as a to-buy list item.

wishlist_role.label: gift_planning
wishlist_role.definition: Saved for someone else / a gift.

wishlist_role.label: comparison_shortlist
wishlist_role.definition: Saved specifically to compare against other candidates.

wishlist_role.label: unclear
wishlist_role.definition: Record doesn't clearly support a specific wishlist-use reason, or doesn't concern wishlist saving at all.

purchase_intent.label: genuine_intent
purchase_intent.definition: Explicit/strongly implied plan to actually purchase this specific item.

purchase_intent.label: consideration
purchase_intent.definition: Actively weighing whether to buy, not yet decided.

purchase_intent.label: bookmarking
purchase_intent.definition: Saved for later reference/tracking with no stated purchase plan.

purchase_intent.label: inspiration
purchase_intent.definition: Saved for style/mood-board purposes, no purchase intent implied.

purchase_intent.label: unclear
purchase_intent.definition: Not enough evidence to classify intent.

purchase_outcome.note: The decision outcome only -- NOT what happened after purchase (see post_purchase). A returned item is still 'purchased' here; the return lives in post_purchase.issues and journey_stage=return_exchange.

post_purchase_issue_types.label: fit_quality_problem
post_purchase_issue_types.definition: Wrong size, poor fit, or quality defect on the received item.

post_purchase_issue_types.label: customer_service_problem
post_purchase_issue_types.definition: Poor support experience (unresponsive, unhelpful, refused resolution).

post_purchase_issue_types.label: wrong_item
post_purchase_issue_types.definition: Received a different item than ordered.

post_purchase_issue_types.label: other
post_purchase_issue_types.definition: Any other post-purchase problem not covered above.

future_purchase_relevance.note: Only mark direct/indirect when the text itself supports it -- a quote is required for direct/indirect or the label is downgraded to unclear during validation.

values.label: direct
values.definition: Text explicitly states an effect on future purchasing/shopping behavior.
values.worked_example: "Wrong size delivered, exchange refused, never ordering from Myntra again." -> direct (explicit refusal to order again).

values.label: indirect
values.definition: Text strongly implies a forward-looking effect without stating it as explicitly as 'direct' cases -- e.g. trust language, hedged future statements.
values.worked_example: "After that experience I'll think twice before ordering anything I can't try in store." -> indirect.

values.label: none
values.definition: Text is post-purchase feedback with no future-purchase implication, positive or negative.
values.worked_example: "Love the dress, fits perfectly." -> none (positive post-purchase feedback, not a stated future-purchase effect either way).

values.label: unclear
values.definition: A post-purchase problem is stated but the text does not say whether it affects future purchasing.
values.worked_example: "Wrong size delivered." -> unclear (a problem occurred; effect on future purchasing not stated).

external_research_channels.label: cross_retailer_listing
external_research_channels.definition: Checked the same/similar product on another retailer.

external_research_channels.label: offline_store
external_research_channels.definition: Checked or tried the product in a physical store.

external_research_channels.label: social_media_post
external_research_channels.definition: General social media mention/discussion, not influencer-specific.
